bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Cardiovascular Perfusionist Salary

A cardiovascular perfusionist operates heart-lung machines during surgery and is a highly skilled health professional. Your pay is usually set by the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020** (MA000027) or by an enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) provide the minimum hourly rates for each classification level under this award. Because the search results do not list a specific cardiovascular perfusionist salary, you should refer to the award classification that matches your qualifications and experience.

### Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The standard full-time week under most modern awards is **38 hours**. To estimate your annual gross pay:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, if your hourly rate is $50:
- Weekly: $50 × 38 = $1,900
- Fortnightly: $1,900 × 2 = $3,800
- Annual: $1,900 × 52 = $98,800

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time, use your agreed weekly hours instead of 38.

### Award Rates vs. the National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** (or $33.05 for casuals including 25% loading). A cardiovascular perfusionist salary will almost always be higher than this minimum because of the specialised skills required. The award sets minimum rates for each classification – for example, a Health Professional Level 1 may have a higher minimum than Level 2. Check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual, you are entitled to a **25% loading** on top of the base hourly rate. This loading is paid instead of annual leave, sick leave, and public holiday pay. When using a calculator, never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – instead, enter the base rate and apply the loading separately.

### Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|----------------|-------------------|
| $0 – $18,200 | Nil |
| $18,201 – $45,000 | 15c for each $1 over $18,200 |
| $45,001 – $135,000 | $4,020 + 30c for each $1 over $45,000 |
| $135,001 – $190,000 | $31,020 + 37c for each $1 over $135,000 |
| $190,001+ | $51,370 + 45c for each $1 over $190,000 |

Most residents also pay a **Medicare levy of 2%** of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in the on-site reference. For a more detailed estimate, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **superannuation guarantee** of **12%** of your ordinary earnings on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an additional contribution to your super fund. The maximum earnings base for the super guarantee is **$270,830 per year** (2026–27). For example, if your annual gross is $98,800, your employer will contribute an extra $11,856 to super, provided your earnings are below the cap.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Own Calculations

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: the annual figure is an estimate based on 38 hours per week and the same rate every week. It does not include penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $50/hour example: $1,900 × 2 = $3,800 per fortnight before tax. The [reference tables](/data) include common conversion factors.

### Summary

- A cardiovascular perfusionist salary is typically governed by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award.
- Use the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 to get annual gross.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour; award rates are higher.
- Casual loading adds 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, up to the cap.
- Tax and Medicare levy reduce your take-home pay; use the resident tax scale for 2026–27.

For the most accurate figures, always check your specific award classification and any applicable enterprise agreement.
